statement: The H-Tate calculation has the following properties. (1) The first differential is d5(bm qn ξ) = (m + 2n + 2j)bm+2 qn θ ∧ ξ, ξ ∈ Λj V, up to a single nonzero scalar normalization. Its cohomology has generators A, B = b3, Θ = b−1θ and b−2(V/Kθ) as in (4.11), with µ = 1. For a fixed c ∈ k×, the next differential is d9(Θ) = cA−2 F = cb4 J. Equivalently, on surviving Θ-containing representatives, d9 (︁ [bm qn θ ∧ ξ] )︁ = c[bm+5 qn Jξ], where ξ is a complementary exterior monomial. These raw products are interpreted in the A, B normal form: A−2 is a surviving unit, while b4 and J need not survive separately. Its cohomology is (4.12). (2) The d17 is wedge multiplication by the invariant Hasse vector h, with common unit shifts and coefficients p on exterior degree zero and p − 1 on exterior degree one. Its survivors have supports component p (mod 3) scalars 0 ℓ 2 W/ℓ 1 det W 0. (3) The nonzero d33 contracts ℓ to scalars and det W to W/ℓ. Under the identifications by h and h ∧ (−), respectively, these maps are multiplication by h3, up to nonzero scalar units and the prescribed degree shifts. Only scalars at p ≡ 0 and quotient classes at p ≡ 1 remain, now over S0/(Z) = k. (4) The remaining algebra and differentials are (4.22), (4.27), and (4.28). The coefficient e53 has not been asserted nonzero in this subgroup calculation.
